text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE MUSLIM
- Indian Foreign Secretary Salman Haider said the second round of the secretary-level talks with Pakistan would be "constructive and purposeful".
- A five-member delegation of the U.S. Drug Enforcement Agency is arriving here on Friday for talks with Pakistani authorities on Pakistani-U.S. cooperation in anti-narcotics operations.
THE NATION
- The prime ministers of India and Pakistan exchanged good wishes on the hotline contact established between the two countries on Thursday.
- Chief Minister Sindh, Liaquat Jatoi, said army deployment was not the solution to law and order problems in Karachi.
- Three employees of a factory were gunned down by two unidentified motorcyclists in Lahore.
- Chief Minister Balochistan Sardar Akhtar Mengal denied reports that Aimal Kansi was arrested in Balochistan.
DAWN

- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif and Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral have resolved to normalise strained ties between the two countries as the foreign secretary-level talks begin in Islamabad on Friday, the foreign office said.
- The presidents of three stock exchanges have opposed rules introduced by the state-run Corporate Law Authority seeking to nominate directors of the exchanges.
- The Modaraba Association of Pakistan has asked the government to extend the tax exemption announced for mutual funds to modarabas.
- Export consignments worth millions of dollars for the United States are held up at ports in the absence of government regulations.
- Foreign exchange reserves fell to $1.020 billion on June 14 from $1.064 billion on June 7.
- The government has decided to marginalise the role of the Income Tax department by engaging private chartered accountants the task of auditing the accounts of tax-payers.
- The Accountability Cell has prepared a reference against former prime minister Benazir Bhutto on charges of allotting nine plots in the federal capital in violation of the rules.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The government has decided to give full sales tax refund to exporters within 30 days, rescinding the new formula announced in the 1997/98 (July-June) budget last Friday.
- The government is likely to offer 23 concession sites including five offshore oil and gas exploration blocks for exploration rights within the next few days.
- Business and industry remained at a standstill in Karachi on the third consecutive day of an unofficial strike resulting in a loss of at least three billion rupees ($74 million).
FINANCIAL POST

- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said the banking reforms are aimed at improving working of the sector to enable it to meet the requirements of a growing economy and provide financial services on efficient and modern lines.
($1=40.49 Pakistani rupees)
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
